name: In-Kernel Stream Compaction (InK-Compact)
definition: A stream compaction technique performed immediately within the operating GPU kernel (as a device function) rather than launching separate kernels or calling host-side libraries, designed to reduce bottlenecks and overhead by avoiding kernel synchronization and additional kernel launches.
summary: InK-Compact is a GPU kernel primitive that compacts valid elements into a contiguous array while preserving order, avoiding global memory writes for invalid elements and eliminating inter-kernel dependencies to minimize synchronization overhead.
